T: The Axe Gang is coming. Dinner's not.
D: A small-time crook in 1940s Shanghai tangles with a gang and the hidden kung fu masters of a run-down tenement.
P: Serve the mains when the Landlady comes out in her curlers.
S: the poor tenement where everyone lives
Yeasted dough proved an hour, wrapped around char siu pork chopped with oyster sauce, hoisin and sugar, proved again 20 minutes, steamed 12 minutes.
one of the masters hiding as a baker
Youtiao: dough of flour, baking powder and a little salt rested overnight, two strips pressed together, stretched and fried at 190C until puffed and golden. Warm soy milk to dip.

Clear hard candy lollipops boiled from sugar and glucose, flavoured with lemon and swirled with red and yellow colour, set on baking paper. Line two trays with baking paper and lay out 12 lollipop sticks. Boil 400g sugar, 150ml liquid glucose and 125ml water without stirring until it reaches 150C on a sugar thermometer. Take off the heat and stir in 1 tsp lemon extract. Spoon rounds over the end of each stick, then drag a toothpick dipped in red and yellow colour through each for a swirl. Cool 20 minutes until hard.
1 packet red and yellow food colouring@Pantry
M: the Landlady in curlers, yelling at everyone

Pork and prawn wontons in a clear ginger and chicken broth, on thin egg noodles with choy sum, spring onion and a dash of chilli oil. Mix 250g pork mince with 200g chopped green prawns, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp sesame oil, grated ginger and chopped spring onion. Fill 32 wonton wrappers and fold. Simmer 1.5L chicken stock with sliced ginger and 2 tbsp soy. Boil the wontons for 3 minutes, then cook 400g thin egg noodles for 2 minutes and blanch 2 bunches choy sum. Divide everything into bowls, ladle over the broth and add spring onion and chilli oil.
Axe Gang salt and pepper pork
the gang that dances into every scene
Pork belly in strips coated in potato starch, fried at 180C until crisp, tossed in a wok with garlic, chilli, spring onion and Sichuan salt and pepper. Steamed rice.
W: Sago boiled 15 minutes until clear, rinsed, chilled in coconut milk, topped with blitzed ripe mango and fresh mango cubes.
K: Dried chrysanthemum flowers steeped 5 minutes in hot water with a little rock sugar, served warm or iced.

s.note: the poor tenement where everyone lives
s.how: Mix 400g flour, 7g yeast, 2 tbsp sugar and 220ml warm water and prove an hour. Chop 300g char siu pork with 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp hoisin and 1 tsp sugar. Fill 12 rounds of dough, pleat shut, prove 20 minutes and steam 12 minutes.

s.note: one of the masters hiding as a baker
s.how: Mix 300g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp salt and 200ml water, knead briefly and rest overnight in the fridge. Cut strips, press two together, stretch and fry at 190C until puffed and golden. Serve with warm soy milk.

m.n: Axe Gang salt and pepper pork
m.note: the gang that dances into every scene
m.how: Cut 800g pork belly into strips and toss in 100g potato starch. Fry at 180C until crisp. Wok-toss with 4 sliced garlic cloves, 2 chillies, spring onion and 1 tsp Sichuan pepper ground with salt. Serve with 300g jasmine rice.

w.how: Boil 100g sago for 15 minutes until clear, rinse and chill. Mix with 400ml coconut milk and 3 tbsp sugar. Blitz 1 ripe mango and dice another. Spoon the sago into glasses and top with mango purée and cubes.

d.how: Steep 15g dried chrysanthemum flowers in 1L hot water with 50g rock sugar for 5 minutes. Strain and serve warm in cups, or chill and pour over ice.
